newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela's Matos skirts bolivar valuation debate.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela's Matos skirts bolivar valuation debate.

text.p: Venezuelan Finance Minister Luis Raul Matos Azocar skirted Tuesday questions on the bolivar amid a growing debate as to whether it might be overvalued, arguing that exchange rate policy was properly the Central Bank's domain.
"What's important is that the foreign exchange market continues in its current stability," Matos told reporters outside Congress.
"That's what we have to watch out for ... until the Central Bank takes any decisions, should that be considered necessary, to change the current bands system," he added.
Venezuela established a foreign exchange bands system in July.

A then-central parity of 470 bolivars per dollar was set to depreciate at a monthly rate of 1.5 percent. Bands were also set 7.5 percent either side of the depreciating central rate to provide leeway for the exchange rate to absorb shocks.
But as the bolivar has continued to trade at around 470 per dollar, despite monthly inflation of more than four percent, analysts now say the bolivar is bumping along the bottom band.
Policy options include widening the bands or revaluing the central parity, analysts say.

However, last week economists at the prestigious Caracas-based Institute of Higher Administrative Studies (IESA) said the bolivar was already 15 percent overvalued and is damaging any rebound in non-traditional exports.
